direction: Record who said each message and who each reply is for; never answer from a guess about the speaker.
dont_over_correct: Do not ask "who is that for?" on every message or add a name to every line. Ask only when the asker is unclear. Treat a reply to the bot's message as addressing it.
prompt: In a group, answer only when addressed, name the member whose request you are answering, and ask who a message is for when it is unclear.
design: Pass each human turn to the model as "<display name>: <text>", not "user".
Keep an open-request list per thread (asker, request, status) and close each request when answered.
Never state what a member said unless they said it in the thread.
setup_questions: Which platform fields give the sender ID, mentions and reply-to?
Is the group a support thread with a customer and bystanders, or a group of peers?

evals.behaviour: two members ask the bot different things within a minute
evals.pass_if: two replies, each addressed to its own asker by name, thread or reply-to
evals.fail_if: a reply goes to the last speaker or carries the other member's answer

evals.behaviour: a follow-up could belong to either of two members
evals.pass_if: one short question about who or what it is for
evals.fail_if: a guess, or a long list of questions

evals.behaviour: members talk to each other without addressing the bot
evals.fail_if: a reply to a message that was not for the bot

evals.behaviour: one member addresses the bot with a clear request
evals.pass_if: the answer, with the name or thread once
evals.fail_if: a "who is that for?" question, a name added to every line, or a reply much longer than the answer needs

guardrail.condition: the reply's addressee is not the asker of the request it closes, or the model input has a human turn with no sender name
guardrail.also: asker unclear -> ask_user; two failed clarifying questions in a support thread -> handoff with the open-request list
